Belarusian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle Belarusian бокъ (bok), from Proto-Slavic *bokъ (“side”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [bok]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

бок • (bok) m inan (genitive бо́ку, nominative plural бакі́, genitive plural бако́ў)

  1. side
    Synonym: старана́ (staraná)

Derived terms

Noun

[edit]

бок • (bok) m inan (genitive бо́ка, nominative plural бакі́, genitive plural бако́ў)

  1. flank, side of the torso
  2. slope (of a roof)

Komi-Zyrian

Borrowed from Russian бок (bok).

Pronunciation

  • Rhymes: -ok

Noun

бок • (bok)

  1. side

Kyrgyz

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Turkic *bok. Compare to Southern Altai бок (bok), Kazakh боқ (boq), Turkish bok, etc.

Noun

[edit]

бок • (bok) (Arabic spelling بوق)

  1. feces

Macedonian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bokъ (“side”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [bɔk]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: бок
  • Homophones: бог (bog), Бог (Bog)
  • Rhymes: -ɔk

Noun

[edit]

бок • (bok) m (relational adjective бочен)

  1. side
    лежеше на бок ― ležeše na bok ― he/she was lying sideways
  2. flank

Declension

[edit]
Declension of бок
singular plural
indefinite бок (bok) бокови (bokovi)
definite unspecified бокот (bokot) боковите (bokovite)
definite proximal боков (bokov) боковиве (bokovive)
definite distal бокон (bokon) боковине (bokovine)
vocative боку (boku) бокови (bokovi)
count form — бока (boka)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • (adjective): бочен (bočen)
  • (adverb): бочно (bočno)

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak bok, from Proto-Slavic *bokъ. For the sense of "page", compare Serbo-Croatian страна / strana.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈbɔk]
  • Rhymes: -ɔk
  • Hyphenation: бок

Noun

[edit]

бок (bok) m inan

  1. side
    Synonym: страна (strana)
    з правого боку ― z pravoho boku ― on the right side
    лєжац на боку ― lježac na boku ― to lie on one's side
    бок сланїни ― bok slanjini ― side of bacon
  2. page (of a book or other paper bound document)
  3. (computing, Internet) page, web page
    Coordinate term: сайт (sajt)
    главни бок ― hlavni bok ― main page
  4. (anatomy) flank
  5. bulwark

Usage notes

[edit]
  • The sense of a side in geometry (e.g. sides of a triangle) is more often expressed with страна (strana).

Declension

[edit]
Declension of бок (bok)
singular plural
nominative бок (bok) боки (boki)
genitive боку / бока (boku / boka) бокох (bokox)
dative боку (boku) боком (bokom)
accusative бок (bok) боки (boki)
instrumental боком (bokom) боками (bokami)
locative боку (boku) бокох (bokox)
vocative боку (boku) боки (boki)

Russian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • бокъ (bok) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bokъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [bok]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ok

Noun

[edit]

бок • (bok) m inan (genitive бо́ка, nominative plural бока́, genitive plural боко́в, relational adjective боково́й, diminutive бочо́к, augmentative бочи́на)

  1. side (various senses)
    на́ бок ― ná bok ― sideways
    бок о́ бок ― bok ó bok ― side by side
    под бо́ком ― pod bókom ― close by
    на боку́ ― na bokú ― on one side

Derived terms

[edit]

Compound words:

  • бокопла́в m anim (bokopláv)

  • кособо́кий (kosobókij)
  • кособо́чить impf (kosobóčitʹ)
    • перекособо́чить pf (perekosobóčitʹ)
    • перекособо́читься pf (perekosobóčitʹsja)
    • кособо́читься pf (kosobóčitʹsja)
    • скособо́читься pf (skosobóčitʹsja)
  • лежебо́ка m anim or f anim (ležebóka)
  • однобо́кий (odnobókij)

Compounds:

  • вы́йти бо́ком pf (výjti bókom)
  • каки́м бо́ком (kakím bókom)
  • намя́ть бока́ pf (namjátʹ boká)
  • с бока припёка (s boka pripjóka), с боку припёку (s boku pripjóku), сбо́ку припёка (sbóku pripjóka), сбо́ку припёку (sbóku pripjóku)

  • подбочи́ться pf (podbočítʹsja)
  • сбо́ку (sbóku)

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bokъ.

Noun

[edit]

бо̏к m inan (Latin spelling bȍk)

  1. side
    бок уз бок ― side by side
  2. flank

Declension

[edit]
Declension of бок
singular plural
nominative бок бокови
genitive бока бокова
dative боку боковима
accusative бок бокове
vocative боку бокови
locative боку боковима
instrumental боком боковима

Interjection

[edit]

бок (Latin spelling bok)

  1. (Croatia) hi
  2. (Croatia) bye

Southern Altai

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Turkic *bok. Cognate to Kyrgyz бок (bok), etc.

Noun

[edit]

бок • (bok)

  1. feces

Tuvan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Turkic *bok (“dirt”). Cognate to Turkish bok (“faeces”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pɔq/

Noun

[edit]

бок • (bok) (definite accusative бокту, plural боктар)

  1. garbage
